newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Boomers will depart for their tour of the United States in November, despite the fact this will clash with the completion of the National Basketball League's best-of-three grand final series. In the worst scenario for the major scheduling onflict, five players from Adelaide and Melbourne will be forced to miss the start of the tour. P21.

Eagle Farm horse trainer Barry Baldwin will face a stewards inquiry, and possibly a fine, for taking the wrong horse to the Beaudesert Fillies and Mares Maiden race. Baldwin took four-year-old Royal Georgia instead of Snow Mass in a mix-up that was discovered by cadet steward Wade Birch. P21.

Super league and the Australian Rugby League are blaming each other for breakdowns in peace talks. Both sides have attempted to positively promote themselves, but the continuing conflict has ruled out any hope for fans for a single competition next year. P22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby Union chief executive John O'Neill says a battle over beer-selling rights is another obstacle, along with Australian Football League opposition, that is preventing rugby union from returning to the Melbourne Cricket Ground. P46.

Australian tennis captain John Newcombe has welcomed the inclusion of Pete Sampras and Michael Chang in the US team for the Davis Cup semi-final against Australia. Newcombe believes that changes to the US team will give Australia an edge in team spirit at the Cup in September. P47.

Former Australian Cricket Board chairman and Ashes team manager Alan Crompton has been voted off the board of the New South Wales Cricket Association. Former vice-president Roger Wotton has also been replaced by Trevor Wholohan. P48.
THE AGE

International and Australian athletes at the Perth cycling championships will be subjected to blood and urine drug tests as of next week. The testing program is the result of an initiative by the world cycling body, UCI, in an effort to combat the killer drug erythropoetin. PB16.

North Melbourne Australian Football League player Anthony Rock is likely to miss the final two home-and-away games due to a knee injury. Injured during the first few minutes of last Sunday's match against Richmond, Rock is not expected to resume full training until next week. PB16.

Western Bulldogs Australian Football League coach Terry Wallace is rallying fans to show up to Saturday's match against the West Coast Eagles, which is the final match at Whitten Oval. Wallace has urged fans to show a massive amount of home support and to make West Coast feel as uncomfortable as possible. PB16.
THE HERALD SUN

Geelong Australian Football League player Gary Ablett will not be able to make a decision as to his playing future until the end of the year. Ablett's manager Ricky Nixon says it is impossible to speculate on the player's career while he recovers from a knee reconstruction. P78.

Australian Football League Collingwood coach Tony Shaw says he will resign at the end of the 1998 season unless the club's on field-performance improves. Shaw also maintains he will not accept payment for the final year of his contract in 1999. P80.

Champion jockey Wayne Harris has reclaimed his title as one of Australia's best jockeys after winning double at Kembla George yesterday with Antiquity and Trifein. The win comes less than a year after Harris fought for his life against a brain tumour. P80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Officials for the Brisbane Broncos are appealing to the Super League to reduce a grade two dangerous tackle charge against Steve Renouf to avoid a three-match suspension, and enable him to play in the grand final at the ANZ Stadium in September. P69.

Australian Rugby League players Jack Elsegood and John Cross won't know for another week whether they will be able to join Super League clubs, or whether they will be forced to remain with the ARL. Supreme Court Judge William Windeyer hopes to hand down is decision next week. P69.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor and coach Geoff Marsh have selected Tasmanian all rounder Shaun Young has as the third seamer for the final Test of the Ashes tour, replacing NSW's Shane Lee. P70.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
